main_text.l: DOctarum potis ElegantiarumBeza magnificas referre laudes,Pocillum artificis sagacioreMitto Dædalei manu politum:Vicinio tui fauente torno.Quod vix excipiat cauo pusilloFlentis lachrymulam unicam puelli.Quod vix ventriculo queat minutoRoris exiguam tenere guttam.Quo formica suam labore fessaIugi paruula vix sitim leuarit.Quo nec florilega sagax proboscisMergi possit apis calente sole:Nec arguta semel cicada siccasCantu perpetuo rigare fauces.Vix illo valeat culex iacere,Aut pulex tenuis latere totus.O si tam modicis, minutulisquePauxillo madidis mero cululisDecertare modo iuuaret acresPotores: neque poculo liceretProuocare viros capaciore!Laudarent Sapido politioresVates Teutonici suos: nec vnquamTam charis biberent merum popinis.

page.notes: The slip pasted at the foot carries the last line of verse and the letter "E" at its right; the slip's text is transcribed as printed. Initial D of the first stanza is a large decorative capital, joined to "Octarum". Several doubtful readings in the verse (e.g. "Vicinio", "cululis") are uncertain.
